approach: Add a `bug-evidence` default to defaults.toml. Add `ensure_bug_evidence(reading, request_text)` in reading.rs beside `ensure_changelog`, called from `build_reading` before `validate()`. For a `change` reading it adds one content criterion (data-backed root-cause evidence) and one `bug-evidence` defaults_applied entry, once. Two-tier trigger. Tier 1: the reader listed `bug-evidence` in defaults_applied, unless that entry's `how` says it does not apply. Tier 2, a narrow fallback: a bug word within two words of a fix-intent word, in the request text or the reading title (not the summary). The step's criterion is skipped only when its own lead phrase is already present, so a standing-default criterion such as 'root-cause: the change description names the root cause' never suppresses it. The reader prompt set is 3 tokens under budget, so `BudgetSet::Reader` in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs must rise. That is a forced deviation, not an athena.toml key. The raise is recorded as a new appended decision D166 that amends D25 without editing it (the log is append-only), and not by amending D25. The reading's athena.toml deliverable stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: Add the criterion and defaults entry as a step in `build_reading` next to `ensure_changelog`, not as a refusal in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: Root cause: bug jobs were rejected at the final verdict because no criterion demanded data-backed root-cause evidence. A step guarantees the criterion with no model round trip, refuses nothing (no replay refusal rate, no new `step!` line, no new corpus case), and follows `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:281-303): idempotent, capability-gated, run before `validate()`.

rejected.why: It adds a refusal rule (replay share, a corpus case that must refuse) and sends the reader round again for a sentence Athena can write itself.

rejected.option: Rely on the reader prompt and the default alone
rejected.why: Prose-only; the `mechanism` default asks for enforcement by mechanism.

decisions.choice: Two-tier trigger, applied only when `capability == Some("change")`. Tier 1: a defaults_applied entry with id `bug-evidence` whose lowercase `how` contains none of 'not applicable', 'does not apply', "doesn't apply", 'n/a', 'not a bug'. Tier 2: `names_bug_work(text)` is true for the request text or for the reading title. `names_bug_work` lowercases, replaces 'wrong output' with 'wrong-output', splits on whitespace and trims non-alphanumeric characters from each token's ends (inner hyphens stay). Bug tokens: bug, bugs, regression, regressions, slowdown, slowdowns, wrong-output. A `regression` token followed by test, tests or testing is skipped. Fix tokens: fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, repair, repairs, repaired, diagnose, investigate. It is true when a bug token and a fix token have at most two tokens between them, in either order. The tokens `bug-fix` and `bugfix` count alone, since they already state fix intent. A compound such as `bug-evidence` or `bug_id` is a different token and matches nothing. A negated tier-1 entry suppresses tier 1 only; tier 2 still decides.
decisions.reason: Finding 7: a bare fix word anywhere still matched 'Fix the docs for the bug report form' and 'Fix a typo in the regression section'. The two-token window rejects both (four tokens lie between), while 'Fix the regression', 'Fix the long-standing regression in X' and 'Investigate the slowdown' pass. Finding 10: reader.md:17 asks for 'each default below that applies, with how', and `applies_to` is `*`, so a reader may list the default with a 'how' that says it does not apply; the negation list ignores that listing, and a test pins it. Tier 1 otherwise trusts the reader's semantic judgement, which is the only check that sees paraphrases. `class_of_work` is a closed list (athena.toml:128-129) with no bug class. `build_reading` has no request today (reading.rs:685-695), so one `&str` argument is added; its callers are reading.rs:642 and the test helper at reading.rs:5630. On a retry such as this job's request 'try again on 20261105-234147-88tw', the request text carries no bug word, so tier 2 relies on the reader's title alone (finding 8), and tier 1 relies on the reader naming the default. This job's own title has no fix verb, so only tier 1 covers it. The limits go in the doc comment and defaults-loop.md §3.9.

decisions.reason: Finding 6: the standing `root-cause` default (defaults.toml:77-78, applies_to `*`) makes readers write a criterion such as 'root-cause: the change description states why...'. risks.risk: The fallback misses a bug request with no listed bug word (for example 'fix the crash') or fires on a feature request with both a bug word and a fix word within two tokens (for example 'Fix the bug report form').
risks.mitigation: Tier 1 covers paraphrases because the reader sees the default's first sentence. Tier 2 needs a bug token within two tokens of a fix token, ignores compounds such as bug-evidence, skips 'regression test(s)', and reads only the request and the title. The docs/typo cases are in the negative table; the limits are in the doc comment and §3.9.

risks.risk: A retry request such as 'try again on <id>' has no bug words, so tier 2 misses retries of bug jobs (finding 8; the earlier plan stated this backwards).
risks.mitigation: State in the doc comment and §3.9 that on a retry tier 2 relies on the reading title alone and tier 1 on the reader naming the default. A test pins the title-only positive and the neutral-title negative.

risks.risk: A reader lists `bug-evidence` with a 'how' that says it does not apply, or with an unlisted negation wording, and the criterion is added to a feature reading.
risks.mitigation: Tier 1 ignores an entry whose `how` contains one of the listed negations, pinned by a test. Any other wording is trusted; that limit is documented in the doc comment and §3.9.

risks.risk: The added criterion text trips an existing reading check and refuses the whole reading.
risks.mitigation: The criterion is content kind with no path, no 'only ... may change' phrase and no producer-report wording; `bug_evidence_added_text_trips_no_refusal_check` runs `refusing_check` on the built reading.

risks.risk: The decision-log edit breaks the append-only or entry-structure rules (a D25 edit, a wrong id, a missing Provenance bullet).
risks.mitigation: Append only after the last entry, confirm the highest id with Grep `^## D` before choosing the next, use the D165 bullet shape, and leave D25 unedited. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` and the refusal_corpus test.

risks.mitigation: Step 10 greps for '1997', '99.85' and 'of 2000' in the touched docs and crates and fixes each reader figure; the older 1,930 history stays.

risks.risk: The step guarantees the criterion exists, not that the producer meets it; the final verdict is still the verifier's judgement, and its rejection logic is out of scope.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and §3.9 say so. The default requires readable data and says an estimate-labelled guess does not meet it, which gives the verifier an explicit test.

risks.risk: One more criterion means one more demonstration for the planner on every bug reading, including readings where the reader wrote its own root-cause criterion.
risks.mitigation: This is intended (finding 6): a standing-default criterion does not require readable data. It is documented in §3.9.

demonstrations.method: Parse the repo defaults.toml in an athena-data unit test and check the new entry's id, applies_to, key phrases and source. The test also asserts the `root-cause` statement equals its base text.
demonstrations.observes: `bug_evidence_default_parses_and_renders_its_first_sentence` passes. It asserts: applies_to is ["*"]; the statement contains 'before any fix', 'root cause', 'data the job can read' and 'a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet this'; the source contains 20261104-054700-e6js, 20261105-051344-q9fv, 20261105-101121-qw9r and 20261105-205835-hk09; the `root-cause` statement is byte-identical to the base.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the defaults.toml entry `get("bug-evidence")` is None and the test fails; a reworded `root-cause` fails the equality assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production `DefaultsModel::parse` and `get` (crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs:36, 51) on the real file through the existing `REPO_DEFAULTS` const (defaults.rs:89). Exists; no double. The test is added by step 2.

demonstrations.method: Grep reading.rs for `bug-evidence`, and run a source-text test (the style of the existing include_str! tests at reading.rs:9241 and 10944) that takes the body of `build_reading` and asserts the call order.
demonstrations.observes: Grep for `bug-evidence` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows the id constant and the entry. The test asserts that `build_reading`'s body contains `ensure_changelog(&mut reading)`, then `ensure_bug_evidence(&mut reading, request_text)`, then `reading.validate()`, in that order, and that `ensure_bug_evidence` returns early unless capability is `change`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Removing the call from `build_reading`, or moving it after `validate()`, makes the test fail.
demonstrations.seam: Reads the production source of reading.rs with `include_str!` and splits at `fn build_reading(`, as the existing source-text tests do. Exists in style; the new test is added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests drive the real `Athena::build_reading` through a new helper with bug requests, and call the step directly over positive and negative tables. They cover both tiers, the negated tier-1 entry, the standing-default criterion, the retry-by-title case, idempotency, and that the added text trips no `refusing_check` step.
demonstrations.observes: All `bug_evidence_*` tests pass. (a) A change reading built from request 'Fix the bug where the report shows the wrong output' has exactly one content criterion starting 'Before any fix, the change states the root cause' and exactly one `bug-evidence` entry; `refusing_check` on it is None. (b) Fallback positives: 'Fix the regression in the parser', 'Investigate the slowdown in queue drain', 'Fix wrong-output in the status line', 'Fix the regression and add a regression test', 'Bugfix for the parser crash'. Fallback negatives, which get neither the criterion nor the entry: 'Add a regression test for the parser', 'Add bug-evidence default and enforce root-cause criterion on bug', 'Throughput review: flag median slowdowns and queue a request', 'Fix the docs for the bug report form', 'Fix a typo in the regression section of the README', 'Describe the demo in README.md', 'Add debug logging', a study-capability bug request, a declined reading. (c) Tier 1: a change reading whose request has no keyword but whose defaults_applied lists `bug-evidence` gains the criterion and no second entry. A tier-1 reading whose only root-cause criterion is 'root-cause: the change description names the root cause' still gains the step's criterion. A reader entry whose `how` is 'not applicable: this is not a bug job' on a feature request gains no criterion. (d) Retry: request 'try again on 20261105-234147-88tw' with title 'Fix the regression in the parser' gains the criterion through the title; the same request with a neutral title gains nothing. (e) Calling the step twice leaves the reading equal.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no step, (a) finds zero root-cause criteria and zero `bug-evidence` entries. With bare `has_phrase` matching, the negative table fails on 'bug-evidence', 'regression test' and 'slowdowns'. With a fix word allowed anywhere, the docs and typo cases fail. If condition (b) of the earlier plan were kept, the standing-default case in (c) finds no criterion. Without the negation check the 'not applicable' case gains a criterion. With a non-idempotent step, (e) finds duplicates. Without the capability gate, the study case gains the criterion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::build_reading` (reading.rs:685) through a new test helper `build_for_request(reading_json, request_text, capabilities)` added in step 7. It copies `build_sized` (reading.rs:5606-5640): `crate::test_support::make_athena` on tempdirs, the shipped athena.toml and defaults.toml, `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`, capabilities ["change","study"]. The reading JSON comes from the existing `sized_reading` (reading.rs:5580) with capability set to change. The step is also called directly on the existing `change_reading()` (reading.rs:6130). No double holds the logic under test: the real `build_reading`, `names_bug_work` and `refusing_check` run.

demonstrations.method: An athena-data unit test parses the repo defaults.toml and checks the entry and its rendered first-sentence line.
demonstrations.observes: `DefaultsModel::parse` succeeds on the real file. `render()` contains the exact line `- bug-evidence [*]: <first sentence>\n` and does not contain the statement's second sentence.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the entry the line is absent. If the first sentence had no '. ' break, the render would carry the whole statement and the second-sentence assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production `DefaultsModel::parse`, `get` and `render` (defaults.rs:36, 51, 58) on the real file through `REPO_DEFAULTS` (defaults.rs:89). Exists; no double.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks, the budget tests that compose the reader set from the real defaults.toml, the briefs and pin tests that quote the reader figure, and the refusal corpus. Existing tests keep their outcomes.
demonstrations.observes: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` pass. `cargo test --locked` passes, including `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` (`every_role_set_is_within_its_budget`, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`), the run_pin_tests.rs:1624-1644 test now reading `BudgetSet::Reader.budget()`, the decision-entry structure tests, and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. The corpus adds no case: the step refuses nothing. That test reads docs/decisions.md for D164 (line 652) and D165 (line 1186) by `split_once` and `contains`, which the appended D166 leaves true; I read those lines and cite no result.
